native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (while becoming insignifcant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: The variable is SAMPLE_RACE — specifically the Black-versus-White contrast in the effect of race on BA degree completion. In logit models on the full sample (n = 8,773; 2.69% complete a BA), the Black coefficient is large and highly significant before adjustment (-1.006, p < 0.0001, race only; -0.862, p < 0.0001, adding SES alone), but once BOTH SES and academic characteristics (the ASVAB composite and class percentile) are included, the Black effect shrinks to 0.0926 (SE 0.225) and becomes statistically insignificant (p = 0.68). This is the only variable, coding, and specification in the data that reproduces the reported 0.0923 value (|difference| < 0.001) with p > 0.05; no other candidate (Hispanic, Female/Male, SES, family size) comes close, and the same attenuation-to-insignificance holds in probit (Black = 0.074, p = 0.45; 0.094, p = 0.32 without the Hispanic dummy). We could not reproduce the companion 0.5024 figure under any model (logit, probit, linear-probability, marginal effects) or racial coding in this file — likely it comes from a reference-analysis stage that used a curriculum variable documented for the dataset but absent from the processed CSV — so the conclusion rests on the exact 0.0923 match plus the unique race-contrast attenuation pattern. Substantively: the Black-White gap in BA attainment is explained away by socioeconomic status and academic characteristics (ability and class standing); after adjusting for both, the residual racial effect is statistically zero.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Data inspection (n=8,773, no NaN, unique CASE IDs, 2.69% BA, 3 race / 2 sex levels). 2) Staged logit models A (background only) / B (+SES) / C (+SES+ABILITY+PERCENTILE) with coef/SE/p tables for all SAMPLE_RACE and SAMPLE_SEX contrasts; FAMILY SIZE sensitivity variant. 3) Coding/scaling variants (White, Minority, NonBlack, SES, FAM, z-scores). 4) Exhaustive search: 9 candidates x all control subsets x {logit, probit} (~4,600 models) matching 0.5024 and 0.0923 (|Δ| thresholds); unique match: logit Black = 0.092592 (p=0.680) in BA ~ Black+Hispanic+SES+ABILITY+PERCENTILE. 5) Bounded scale/sign check: LPM, MEM and AME of the race contrast (4 codifications x 3 stages, 84 estimates) — 0.5024 not reproducible under any scale or coding; positive codings (White/NonBlack) give +0.97/+0.80 in A/B and +0.074 in C, never +0.0923. Conclusion therefore rests on the 0.0923 match and the attenuation-to-insignificance pattern for race only.
